questions.question:
D4 — Issue 1 [P1] (confidence 9/10) PLAN.md:19-20: AuthBroker and SessionMint share a global mutable AuthCache via module-level export, and both mutate it.
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count on main — Section 1 Architecture, Multi-tenant Auth Refactor.
ELI10: Two services write to the same cache through a global variable. The plan also says the cache 'does not serialize mutations' (PLAN.md:10). So writes can interleave: SessionMint stores a session while AuthBroker invalidates the same tenant on logout, and the last writer wins with no ordering. A module-level export also means tests share one instance, so one test's leftover token can make another pass or fail. Search check [Layer 1]: dependency injection is the standard cure; module singletons are the documented trap.
Stakes if we pick wrong: a revoked token stays valid for one tenant because a concurrent mint re-wrote it, and no test can reproduce it because the shared instance hides ordering.
Recommendation: 1A because a single instance is fine, a global accessor is not. Inject it once from the composition root and give the facade a narrow write API that owns ordering. Maps to your 'explicit over clever' preference.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=6/10, C=2/10.
Net: one extra constructor parameter per service buys deterministic writes and isolated tests.

options.label: 1A) Inject AuthCache; narrow write API with per-key ordering (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Both services receive the one AuthCache instance via constructor; the module export goes away (human: ~1 day / CC: ~20 min). ✅ AuthCache exposes only get/put/invalidate keyed by a typed TenantKey and serializes writes per key, so mint-vs-revoke ordering is defined and testable. ❌ Every call site that imported the global must be threaded through the composition root.

options.label: 1B) Keep the module export; make SessionMint read-only
options.description: ✅ Smaller change: only AuthBroker writes, so no two-writer race exists (human: ~2 hrs / CC: ~5 min). ✅ Keeps the existing import shape for callers. ❌ Test isolation problem remains, and SessionMint still needs a write path for new sessions, which pushes the race into AuthBroker.

options.label: 1C) Proceed as written
options.description: ✅ Zero re-planning; matches the current draft. ✅ Fastest path to a first commit. ❌ Ships an auth cache with two unordered writers and shared test state on a multi-tenant path.

answers.D4 \u2014 Issue 1 [P1] (confidence 9/10): 1A) Inject AuthCache; narrow write API with per-key ordering (recommended)
